newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden sees '97 borrowing need at 20-30 bln Skr.
newsitem.headline: Sweden sees '97 borrowing need at 20-30 bln Skr.

text.p: Sweden's national debt office forecast on Tuesday the Swedish government borrowing requirement will be 20-30 billion crowns ($4 billion) in 1997, unchanged from its last forecast.
The office also estimated the borrowing requirement for April at one billion crowns and revised its March estimate to six billion crowns, from five billion in its previous forecast.
It said in a statement that it had a financing surplus of 25.3 billion crowns in February, helped by the sale of the government's 34 percent stake in mortgage lender Stadshypotek.

"The borrowing requirement for February was some 16 billion crowns lower than forecast, partly due to the proceeds from the state's sale of shares in Stadshypotek and unexpectedly large supplementary tax payments," it said.
The requirement for the 12 months to February 28 was 15.3 billion crowns, it added.
April state debt issuance was foreseen as 14 billion crowns in T-bills and four billion in bonds while March issuance would be 24 billion crowns in T-bills and four billion in bonds.
The February figure indicates a financing surplus.
